text:
**My pick for a slim Qi2 power bank for the iPhone 17 is the Anker Nano Power Bank (5K, MagGo, Slim).** I couldn't confirm a few details, which I note below.

**Anker Nano Power Bank, 5,000mAh, about $55**
- **Specs:** Anker's page lists it at 0.34 in (8.6 mm) thick and 4.3 oz (122 g). Wireless output is up to 15W for iPhone 12 through 17.
- **Review verdict:** 9to5Mac calls it the closest alternative to Apple's own MagSafe battery and says it runs cooler than competitors.
- **Caveat on Qi2 status:** Anker's page is inconsistent. One place says "Qi2-Certified," another says "Qi2-Compatible," and the output table lists 5W max for wireless. Check the listing before you buy.
- **Caveat on recalls:** The page has a generic "Product Recalls" link in the footer. I couldn't confirm the status for this model.
- **Real capacity:** Anker says you'll get about 2,750 to 3,500mAh delivered to your phone. That's less than a full iPhone charge.
- [Buy at Anker](https://www.anker.com/products/a1665-5k-ultra-slim-qi2-power-bank)

**Other options**
- **UGREEN 10,000mAh, Qi2.2 up to 25W, $59.99:** It isn't as thin, but it has more capacity and 30W wired charging. It also has a built-in USB-C cable. Qi2.2 needs an iPhone 16 or later, so the iPhone 17 qualifies. 9to5Mac is my source for this, and I don't have a link to the product page.
- **Baseus 5,000mAh, $24.99:** It's the cheapest and similarly thin to the Anker. But it has no Qi2 and charges wirelessly at only 7.5W. 9to5Mac is my source for this too, and I have no product link.
- **Baseus PicoGo AM52, 10,000mAh, Qi2.2, 45W:** It's listed at $59.99, or $53.99 with code AM52. The code was tested in Baseus's cart on 2026-10-24, per a deal site. I couldn't verify its thickness or weight. [Deal page](https://dealectric.com/go/baseus-picogo-am52-qi2-2-10000mah-45w)
- **Belkin 25W, 10,000mAh, $99.99:** 9to5Mac calls it "a little chunky," so it isn't a slim pick.
- **LISEN P601, 5,000mAh, 0.38 in:** It's Qi2 certified, but the page only offers bulk orders with a 100-unit minimum. It isn't practical for an individual buyer.

**What I couldn't check**
- The Android Central roundup of 2026 slim Qi2 banks (Baseus, TORRAS, INIU, ReelCharge) didn't load, so I can't compare those models.
- I also didn't read the Macworld and WIRED guides.

**Which to choose:** If you want the slimmest option that charges at full Qi2 speed, get the Anker Nano. If you want more battery and can accept a thicker pack, get a 10,000mAh Qi2.2 model like the UGREEN or Baseus PicoGo.

- **Belkin:** It has a secondary MagSafe ring for attaching accessories, a kickstand, and an LED capacity display. The secondary ring doesn't support charging, so the battery itself must be charged with a cable.

- **iPhone 17:** The article doesn't name a single iPhone 17 pick.
